reasons: Lake identity is verified, non-stub, and matches State v. Mansor, Oregon Supreme Court, decided 2018-06-28.
Lake citations include official cite 363 Or. 185 and parallel cite 421 P.3d 323.
Lake treatment field reports field_i_validity as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
residual_risks: Treatment derivation has an unresolved top-cited audit flag, but no disclosed final point override or final superseding event appears in the lake record.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep live-law claims tied to the treatment caveat noted for the treatment assertion.

reasons: Lens B found no treatment or currency defect that would make placement on Plain View Doctrine stale or legally dead.
The case remains marked good_law in the lake treatment field.
residual_risks: Home-role fit and support are Lens A issues and were not independently reviewed here.

reasons: Lens B found no disclosed overrule, abrogation, supersession, or final limitation that would make the holding statement legally dead.
Lake treatment reports good_law and no point_overrides.
residual_risks: Holding support and quote fidelity are outside Lens B and were not attacked here.

defect.problem: The good_law field matches the lake judgment field, but the page presents the treatment as clean and unconditional even though the lake derivation flags an unresolved top-cited treatment audit and proposed negative events.
defect.proposed_fix: Retain good_law only with a caveat that an R15/top-cited treatment audit is outstanding, or complete that audit before displaying an unconditional good-law status.

reasons: The page treatment fields match lake.treatment: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, varies_by_point false, and the Article I, section 9 scope note.
The same lake record lists 26 proposed treatment edges, including proposed overruled/abrogated/questioned labels, and lane2_top_cited has cap_hit true plus audit_needed true.

Because the negative edges are proposed, point null, and field_iii mentioned, the disclosed record does not prove Mansor is overruled; it does prove the unconditional treatment display needs an audit caveat.
residual_risks: The proposed negative edges may be false positives, but the disclosed record does not include enough adjudicated treatment detail to clear the audit flag.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Display: good_law as of 2026-06-30 per lake judgment; R15/top-cited treatment audit outstanding.

reasons: Lake identity shows Oregon Supreme Court, court_level state.
Lake treatment scope_note says the decision is under Article I, section 9 of the Oregon Constitution, not the Fourth Amendment.
For a federal search-and-seizure corpus, the disclosed state-constitutional scope supports a persuasive, state illustrative weight label.
residual_risks: The lake record does not expose authority_weight as its own field, so the label is inferred from court level and scope note.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the state-constitutional scope note adjacent to the weight label.
